claims.statement: All database access funnels through a single Spring bean: DAOImpl is annotated @Repository("dao"), extends Spring's HibernateTemplate and overrides only setSessionFactory under @Resource(name="sf"), while ServiceDelegateDAO holds it in an @Resource(name="dao") field and mirrors the template API to every service.

The SessionFactory reaches the DAO by name twice: DAOImpl's own @Resource(name="sf") setter override, and ServiceDelegateDAO.setSessionFactory, which is also annotated @Resource(name="sf") and forwards the factory into the DAO instance, so both injections depend on the bean name sf existing.

Because HibernateTemplate (through HibernateAccessor) implements InitializingBean, Spring invokes afterPropertiesSet() on the dao bean and that check rejects a null SessionFactory, so a missing or renamed sf bean fails the container load rather than surfacing on the first query.

Application code never obtains a Hibernate Session: SessionFactory appears only in the DAO's setter and in ServiceDelegateDAO.getSessionFactory(), and no openSession()/getCurrentSession() call exists under src/, so session lifecycle and transaction participation are entirely HibernateTemplate's responsibility.

The HibernateTemplate surface the service layer actually calls is findByCriteria(DetachedCriteria), findByCriteria(DetachedCriteria, first, max), find(hql), find(hql, values), save, get(Class, Serializable), update and delete; the rest of the roughly hundred methods ServiceDelegateDAO mirrors have no call site under src/.

Every generic persistence operation is reachable on any service because all nine @Service beans inherit ServiceDelegateDAO's forwarding methods through BaseServiceImpl, and the underlying HibernateTemplate call is entity-agnostic; that is why deleting a productImage through propertyService still deletes the right row.

BaseServiceImpl resolves the entity class its criteria and HQL target by reflection over its own subclass at construction time, stripping the ServiceImpl suffix and rewriting .service.impl to .pojo into the protected clazz field, and a service whose package or name breaks that convention leaves clazz null after only printing a stack trace.

Reads are DetachedCriteria over Java property names: association properties such as category, product, order and user map to the join columns cid/pid/oid/uid, listByParent derives the property name by uncapitalizing the parent class's simple name, and list(Object...) converts a null value into Restrictions.isNull, which is how "order is null" expresses a cart line.

Counting is done with raw HQL strings rather than criteria: total() concatenates the entity's fully qualified class name into "select count(*) from <FQN>", and total(Object parent) and PropertyServiceImpl.total(Category) append "where bean.<prop> = ?0" and bind the parent entity as a positional parameter, casting the single result to Long.

Paging is an absolute row offset plus a limit: the paged reads pass page.getStart() as firstResult and page.getCount() as maxResults, Page.count defaults to 5, and the admin page links increment page.start by page.count even though the field's comment calls it a page number.

BaseServiceImpl.save casts HibernateTemplate.save's Serializable return value to Integer, which is valid only while the mapped identifier is a primitive int; an entity whose @Id were changed to long/Long would turn its insert path into a ClassCastException.

Nine JPA @Entity classes in com.caozhihu.tmall.pojo are discovered through packagesToScan=com.caozhihu.*; each maps an int id with @GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY) onto an AUTO_INCREMENT primary key, and Order maps to table order_ because order is a reserved word.

With GenerationType.IDENTITY the INSERT must execute while save() runs in order to obtain the generated key, which is why callers read the id immediately after saving: CategoryAction.add builds the category image file name from category.getId() and ForeAction.buyone takes oiid from the freshly saved OrderItem.

Every mapped relationship is a unidirectional @ManyToOne with an explicit @JoinColumn onto cid (product, property), pid (productImage, propertyValue, orderItem, review), ptid (propertyValue), oid and uid (orderItem), uid (order_) and uid (review); no @OneToMany collection is mapped anywhere in the model.

View-only data lives in @Transient fields Hibernate ignores - Category.products/productsByRow, Order.orderItems/total/totalNumber, Product.firstProductImage/productSingleImages/productDetailImages/reviewCount/saleCount - and is populated in memory by service helpers, so those property names can never appear in a criteria or HQL string.

Unannotated fields fall back to the property name as the column name (orderCode, subTitle, userMessage, createDate), which is why the annotations' camelCase table names such as productImage and orderItem line up with the script's lowercase productimage and orderitem; sf configures no Hibernate naming strategy, so a renamed property must be paired with a DDL rename or fail as a runtime SQL error.

Transaction advice exists only at the service layer: a HibernateTransactionManager over bean sf is bound by tx:annotation-driven transaction-manager="transactionManager", and single-entity writes get their boundary from @Transactional(readOnly = false) on ServiceDelegateDAO's save/update/delete/saveOrUpdate and @Transactional on BaseServiceImpl.save, so no action handler needs its own boundary.

Only two flows write more than one entity: OrderServiceImpl.createOrder and ReviewServiceImpl.saveReviewAndUpdateOrderStatus, both annotated @Transactional(propagation = REQUIRED, rollbackForClassName = "Exception"); inside them calls through sibling beans (orderItemService.update, orderService.update) join the same transaction while self-calls on inherited methods open no new one.

The only action-level @Transactional, on PropertyAction.add, is inert because action instances are not Spring beans - Action4Service is the only @Component in the action package and declares no @Action method - while the write it wraps is still transactional through propertyService.save.

No OpenSessionInView filter or interceptor is declared (web.xml declares only struts2 and encodingFilter, and applicationContext.xml declares none), so entities returned by a DAO call are already detached when the JSP renders; that is currently safe only because every mapped association is an eager @ManyToOne and every rendered collection is a @Transient list the services filled in memory, so adding a lazy association would surface LazyInitializationException at render time.

Request flows that read then write are not a single transaction: PropertyValueAction.update stashes the submitted value, re-reads the row through t2p in one template call and then writes through a separate service transaction, holding no lock or snapshot across the two steps.

Handlers that persist a row and write a file are not atomic: CategoryAction.add and ProductImageAction.add commit the saved row before writing (and resizing) the image, and saveWithJpg swallows IOException with a stack trace, so an image failure leaves a committed row whose rendered image source does not exist.

hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto=none means Hibernate never creates or validates the schema, whose only source is dbInit's classpath:sql/tmall_ssh_h2.sql; the script deliberately omits foreign keys that the mapping would otherwise generate, so propertyvalue.pid and orderitem.oid are mapped @ManyToOne columns with no FK constraint.

Request-level reads run outside any transaction boundary: the two interceptors query through the service proxies on every /fore* request (the category list for the search bar, the cart item count), and paging screens issue a count statement and a page statement with no shared snapshot.

TestTmall is the only code that drives DAOImpl directly - it @Autowires the DAO, loads classpath:applicationContext.xml, and its two @Transactional @Test methods build a DetachedCriteria over Category and then delete or save through the DAO - so it is the only check of the dao/sf/dbInit/transactionManager wiring, and nothing runs it automatically.
